name: SELECT2
fullName: Trial of Endovascular Thrombectomy for Large Ischemic Strokes
teachingPoint: Supports EVT for large-core; large core is no longer an automatic exclusion.

name: ANGEL-ASPECT
fullName: Endovascular Therapy for Acute Ischemic Stroke with Large Infarct
teachingPoint: Confirms EVT benefit in large-core population.

name: RESCUE-Japan LIMIT
fullName: Endovascular Therapy for Acute Stroke with Large Ischemic Region
teachingPoint: First major RCT to support large-core EVT.

name: TENSION
fullName: Endovascular Thrombectomy for AIS with Established Large Infarct
teachingPoint: European replication of large-core EVT benefit.

name: LASTE
fullName: Thrombectomy for Stroke with a Large Infarct of Unrestricted Size
teachingPoint: Thrombectomy benefits even very large infarcts (ASPECTS ≤5), at the cost of more sICH.

name: ATLAS
fullName: Endovascular Thrombectomy for Large-Core Ischaemic Stroke up to 24 h — Systematic Review and IPD Meta-analysis with Central Imaging Adjudication
teachingPoint: Consolidates EVT benefit across large-core strata to 24 h, except very extensive cores (≥150 mL) beyond 6 h where evidence remains limited.

name: TESLA
fullName: Thrombectomy for Stroke With Large Infarct on Noncontrast CT
finding: DID NOT meet superiority: UW-mRS 2.93 vs 2.27, adjusted difference 0.63 (95% CrI −0.09 to 1.34); posterior probability .96
teachingPoint: Cautions that NCCT-only ASPECTS 2-5 selection up to 24 h is not clearly beneficial — context for the otherwise positive large-core class.

name: TENSION antithrombotic analysis
fullName: Large Core Stroke Thrombectomy Is Safe and Effective Regardless of Prior Antithrombotic or Thrombolytic Treatment: A Secondary Analysis of the Randomized TENSION Trial
population: n=246, Median 74 (IQR 65-80), Parent TENSION criteria (extended lesion, extended time window); NCT03094715
finding: EVT benefit in every stratum: with antiplatelets cOR 2.40 (1.22-4.99), without 2.29 (1.53-3.46); with anticoagulation cOR 2.45 (1.17-5.28), without 2.12 (1.44-3.15); with IVT cOR 1.46 (0.83-2.61), without 2.89 (1.87-4.51)
teachingPoint: Preadmission antiplatelets or anticoagulants, or prior IV thrombolysis, should not exclude otherwise-eligible large-core patients from thrombectomy — EVT benefit and safety were unmodified by prior antithrombotic exposure.

name: LASTE ASPECTS 0-2
fullName: Endovascular Thrombectomy in Patients With Largest Baseline Infarcts (ASPECTS 0-2): An Ancillary Analysis of the LASTE Trial
population: n=181, Median 72; parent trial capped at <=80, Randomization within 6.5 h of last known well (parent LASTE criteria); NCT03811769
finding: Favored EVT: generalized OR 1.81; mRS 0-3 in 31.4% vs 8.5% (RR 3.69, 95% CI 1.77-7.68)
teachingPoint: In patients under 80 treated within 6.5 h, even ASPECTS 0-2 with a median 156 mL core benefited from EVT — infarct size in isolation should not disqualify thrombectomy, accepting a numerically higher sICH rate for large gains in survival and mRS 0-3.

name: ANGEL-ASPECT HMCAS analysis
fullName: Effects of Computed Tomography Hyperdense Middle Cerebral Artery Sign on the Efficacy of Endovascular Therapy in Acute Ischemic Stroke With Large Infarcts: A Subgroup Analysis of the ANGEL-ASPECT Trial
finding: No significant treatment-by-HMCAS interaction (p=0.19): EVT favored without HMCAS (generalized OR 2.78, 95% CI 1.80-4.27, p<0.001); not statistically significant with HMCAS (adjusted OR 1.69, 95% CI 0.93-3.08, p=0.09)
teachingPoint: The hyperdense MCA sign marks worse prognosis and harder thrombectomy in large-core stroke but showed no significant interaction with EVT benefit — do not use HMCAS to withhold large-core thrombectomy.
